topic: The 1911 Theft of the Mona Lisa

research_dossier.topic: The 1911 Theft of the Mona Lisa
research_dossier.central_question: How did an unassuming carpenter hide inside the Louvre overnight and walk out unnoticed with the most famous painting on Earth?
research_dossier.context: On August 21, 1911, the Mona Lisa was stolen from the Salon Carré of the Louvre, remaining missing for over two years.

chronology.event: Vincenzo Peruggia hides inside a Louvre supply closet overnight.
Peruggia removes painting from frame and walks out into Paris.
Museum guards realize the frame is missing twenty-eight hours later.
Peruggia arrested in Florence attempting to sell the portrait to an antique dealer.

verified_claims.statement: The museum was closed for maintenance when Peruggia took the painting off the wall in broad daylight.
Louvre officials did not realize the painting was stolen until twenty-eight hours after it left the building.
verified_claims.evidence: Contemporary Le Figaro front-page investigative logs.

verified_claims.statement: The painting was hidden in a wooden trunk in a Parisian boarding house for two whole years.
verified_claims.evidence: Italian judicial confession records from Florence trial, 1914.

uncertainties: Whether Peruggia acted alone or had criminal accomplices in the international art trade.
unanswered_questions: Would the Mona Lisa have become world-famous without the international newspaper frenzy of 1911?
research_dossier.notes_for_scriptwriter: Highlight how the museum guards walked past the empty wall assuming photographers had borrowed it.

lines.text: In 1911, an unarmed carpenter walked out of the Louvre with the Mona Lisa.
Vincenzo Peruggia had worked as a glazier at the museum, memorizing guard rotations and security blind spots.
lines.caps: VINCENZO *PERUGGIA | MEMORIZING GUARD *ROTATIONS AND BLIND SPOTS

lines.text: On a quiet Monday morning while galleries were closed, he slipped into a supply closet and waited for silence.
He lifted the wooden panel off the wall, stripped the heavy frame, and concealed the portrait under his coat.
lines.caps: LIFTED *PANEL OFF WALL | CONCEALED PORTRAIT UNDER *HIS COAT

lines.text: Incredibly, museum officials did not notice the empty hooks for more than twenty-four hours, assuming photographers had moved it.
lines.caps: OFFICIALS DID NOT *NOTICE | FOR MORE THAN *TWENTY-FOUR HOURS

lines.text: For two years, the priceless masterpiece sat undisturbed inside a wooden trunk in a humble Parisian boarding house.
lines.caps: PRICELESS *MASTERPIECE | SAT UNDISTURBED IN A *WOODEN TRUNK

lines.text: Peruggia was finally arrested in Florence after attempting to return the stolen treasure to Italian art dealers.
That brazen theft transformed an ordinary museum portrait into the most recognized painting in human history.
lines.caps: BRAZEN *THEFT | MOST RECOGNIZED *PAINTING IN HUMAN HISTORY
